# <a id="_Toc171703911"></a>Purpose

All incidents involving the development environment where a development system or service is down, data loss, or security issue should immediately begin an incident response process to properly notify the appropriate response teams, capture and log all information, contain the incident, provide updates to stakeholders, and track through resolution\. 

​​

# <a id="_Toc171703912"></a>Objective and Scope

The objective of this document is to provide the needed step by step instructions to follow in the event of an automated or manually detected incident\. The overall goal is to protect customers’ data, restore normal service as quickly as possible, and meet both regulatory and contractual compliance requirements\. 

For Teamcenter X, the Deployment and Operations of the customer environments are done by Cloud Application Services \(CApS\) team\. The SRE team is the first line of defence for detecting and responding to uptime affecting incidents\. This is true for all market offerings of Teamcenter X – Essentials, Premium, etc\.

The scope of this document is to cover the incident management process for Teamcenter X and clarify the role of Teamcenter X team in the process\.

# <a id="_Toc171703913"></a>Roles and Responsibilities for this Procedure

Can execute this Procedure

Incident Commander

Yes

The Incident commander should be the primary person to execute this procedure\. This is typically from the SRE team\.

Service Owners an/or SMEs

Yes

In the event there is no Incident Commander, the Service Owners or Operations team members should execute this procedure\. This is from typically from LCS, including Teamcenter X team\.

Operations Engineer

Yes

In the event there is no Incident Commander, the Service Owners or Operations team members should execute this procedure\.

Team Program Managers and Leaders

Yes

If no incident commander, Service Owners, or Operations team member has executed this procedure, the Team Program Managers and leaders should assume the role of Incident Commander and begin executing this procedure\.

# <a id="_Toc171703914"></a>Incident Response Workflow

![A diagram of a business plan

Description automatically generated with medium confidence](data:image/png;base64,)

## <a id="_Toc171703915"></a>Identification \- Automated or manual detection of an incident reported 

1\.1 Automated Incident Identification   
  
Automated notification to the on\-call responder triggered based on configured alarm definitions for infrastructure resources, service operation parameters, and security incidents   
  
Alarm points – currently under review to inventory and ensure proper triggers and trigger sources, alarm names, associated runbooks, team notifications   
  
1\.2 Manual Incident Identification   
  
Manual analysis of logs or dashboards may uncover incidents which require investigation   
  
Example: Reviewing GuardDuty or VPC Flow logs and seeing some unusual activity, which did not trigger an alarm 

## <a id="_Toc171703916"></a>Coordination

### Triage

- 
	1. On\-call responder \(Appendix A – Management Roles\) will evaluate the nature of the incident and assess the severity \(Appendix B – Severity Level Definitions\) to determine the next steps required and initiates the response procedure\. 

### Engage Response Team

- 
	1. Assign an Incident Commander – The on\-call responder will notify the geographic operations team members needed to investigate the issue
	2. Incident commander completes an assessment of known facts\. 
		1. If the Incident Commander determines the incident is security incident the Siemens Cyber Defense incident response process will be followed [https://www\.cert\.siemens\.com/incident\-response/process/](https://www.cert.siemens.com/incident-response/process/)
			1. Contact Siemens DI SW Information Security Officer \(Rich Griener\)
			2. The Siemens Cyber Defense Response Process requires specific coordination across Security Technical expert teams\. It will be the responsibility of the       Incident Commander to ensure the appropriate coordination and notifications are done for the incident and included in the response team as required\.
	3. Incident Commander opens the conference bridge\.
	4. Incident commander designates leads from relevant teams and forms an incident response team\. 
	5. Incident response team evaluates incident and determines the appropriate response effort required\. 

## <a id="_Toc171703917"></a>Resolution

### Investigation

- 
	1. Incident response team gathers key facts about the incident\. 
	2. Additional resources are integrated to allow for expedient resolution\.

### Containment and Recovery 

- 
	1. Identify Subject Matter Experts \(SMEs\) needed\. 
	2. Limit ongoing damage\. 
	3. Fix the underlying issue if possible\. 
	4. Restore affected systems and services to normal operations\. 

### Communication 

- 
	1. Key facts are evaluated to determine whether notification is appropriate\. 
	2. Scribe, IC, or communication lead develops a communication plan with appropriate leads\.

## <a id="_Toc171703918"></a>Closure

### Lessons Learned 

- 
	1. Incident commander adds incident to COE dashboard and identifies incident owners to fully document incident, response effort, and future prevention actions through a root cause analysis process\. 
		1. The COE dashboard is maintained by SRE team in DataDog\.
		2. In addition to that, Teamcenter X team maintains Root Cause Analysis at 
	2. All incidents reviewed formally by the program team once a month\. 

## <a id="_Toc171703919"></a>Improvements

### Program Development 

- 
	1. Maintain the necessary teams training, processes, resources, and tools\. 

### Prevention 

- 
	1. Improve incident response program based on lessons learned\. Use the COE Root Cause Analysis process for every incident to learn from to improve every aspect of the incident response workflow\. 

# Summary

This procedure is intended to ensure an effective incident response plan with all the steps required to react to incidents, determine the scope and risks, and provide the steps for a rapid and thorough response\. 

An executable, step\-by\-step plan will make the response faster and more orderly and will allow the incident response teams to avoid mistakes that could cause damage to the organization, customers, and Siemens brand\. The Incident Response Plan will define how to communicate to stakeholders across all business units and geographies about the risks of an incident, as well as communicating the results of the response\.

# <a id="_Toc171703920"></a>Appendix A \- Incident Management Roles

​​ The following are roles and responsibilities for incident management for Teamcenter X:

Role

Description

Designated Team Members

On\-Call Responder

Reviews and evaluates the nature of the incident report to determine if it represents a system incident 

Operations Engineers based on PagerDuty schedules\.

https://siemenspl\.pagerduty\.com/schedules

Incident Commander \(IC\)

The incident commander initiates Incident Response Procedure and delegates the responsibility for managing different aspects of the incident to the SMEs and manages the incident from the moment of declaration to closure\.

Note: ICs should not become the SMEs for an incident – if required, hand over the IC role to someone else

From SRE team\.

Scribe/Communication Lead

Keeps an accurate timeline of events\. What has happened, when it happened, and the key decisions\. Sends out status to key stakeholders as needed\. 

Anyone can be the scribe, and if no scribe is available, the Incident Commander will assume this role to ensure the incident is being properly documented and communicated\.

Subject Matter Experts \(SMEs\)

Operations Engineers, Developers, Architects, Security Officers

These are the people who will be fixing the problem\. They'll be the ones logging into servers, changing code, and running commands\. The SMEs are the most important role, as nothing would get resolved without them\.

All team members qualify for this role, specifically based on their expertise needed for a given incident and will be called as needed by the Incident Commander or Operations Engineer on call\.

Siemens DI SW Information Security Officer

Rich Greiner

# <a id="_Toc171703921"></a>Appendix B \- Severity Level Definitions 

​​

__Severity Level__ 

__Type of Incident__ 

__Description__ 

__Incident Response Team Required__ 

1 

Emergency – Security Breach, Server Down or Service Unavailable 

Security breach, production is down, or service unavailable, or data integrity issues affecting all users with no immediate workaround identified\. 

Yes 

2 

Critical – Customer Productivity Affected 

Major functionality is impacted or significant performance degradation\. Issue is persistent and affects many users and/or major functionality 

Yes 

3 

Normal – General Problem 

Partial non\-critical loss of software functionality\.    
   
If the incident can be solved by the on\-call Operations Engineer, they will make the needed changes without requiring an Incident Response Team and close the incident\.  

No 

If the incident requires additional Operation Engineers or SMEs support to make changes, the Incident Response Team will be mobilized\. 

Yes 

4 

Low – Informational Notification 

Some action needs to be taken, but can be handled by the Operations team or coordination with the owning service teams 

No
